taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO; native from the southeastern United States through Texas into Mexico and Central America.

evidence: Kew/POWO confirms Texas within the native range.
Regional Lower Colorado/Edwards Plateau planning documents list Helenium quadridentatum as a characteristic native wildflower of the Edwards Plateau region.
Bexar-area roadside/LID native-plant documentation includes longdisk sneezeweed as a native regional species.
Current review did not recover three exact project target-zone county records strong enough to satisfy the project's no-inference rule.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Texas and regional native status are clear, but three exact target-zone counties remain unverified in current evidence.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not convert broad Edwards Plateau or Bexar-region statements into exact county occurrence without explicit county records.

morphology.look_here_first: Treat this as the other winged annual. H. quadridentatum has winged stems and narrow entire distal leaves, but its involucre is usually ovoid to obconic rather than globose. The strongest advanced confirmation is the disc: each disc corolla has 4 lobes, and heads usually have about 10–15 yellow rays.
diagnostic_traits: stems winged by decurrent leaf bases
heads commonly 5–15 or more per plant
ray florets usually 10–15, yellow and fertile
pappus scales non-aristate and very short
often associated with seasonally wet or low sites

confusers.separator: Both are winged annuals with entire distal leaves; H. elegans has globose involucres, while H. quadridentatum is usually ovoid/obconic and has 4-lobed disc corollas.
H. autumnale is perennial with broader often toothed leaves and 5-lobed disc corollas.
H. amarum has no stem wings and much narrower threadlike leaves.

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a project-native taxon until three exact target-zone counties are verified.
